Reviewed all 6 walk-in sore throat visits from 2026-10-01. Five had POSITIVE rapid strep antigen tests (pt-1003, pt-1017, pt-1021, pt-1023, pt-1030); pt-1026 was negative (viral pharyngitis) and received no antibiotic.

Orders placed (all 10-day courses for GAS pharyngitis):
- pt-1003 Maria Lopez (b.1958): amoxicillin 500 mg BID (sulfa allergy only, no beta-lactam issue).
- pt-1017 Maria Lopez (b.1991): amoxicillin 500 mg BID (NKDA, prior amoxicillin tolerated 2023).
- pt-1030 Daniel King: amoxicillin 500 mg BID (NKDA).
- pt-1021 Jennifer Lee: cephalexin 500 mg BID - documented amoxicillin allergy was a benign delayed maculopapular rash (no hives/angioedema/anaphylaxis), so a 1st-generation cephalosporin is appropriate rather than a penicillin.
- pt-1023 Elizabeth Martin: clindamycin 300 mg TID - a 2015 scanned outside urgent care record documents penicillin ANAPHYLAXIS (throat tightness, wheezing, hives within minutes, treated with epinephrine, 2011) that was not on her allergy list. I added "Penicillin" to her allergy list as high criticality with that reaction history, and avoided all beta-lactams. Clindamycin chosen over a macrolide to avoid additive QT risk with her sertraline.

Note: two different patients named Maria Lopez both tested positive; orders were verified against their distinct patient IDs/DOBs.
